headline: High: shared broad network-egress agents can leak CRM/email data into Firecrawl’s web-extraction workflows, with prompt-injection and compliance risks amplified by MCP/API integration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest external content via MCP/direct function calls and touches email/CRM data; firecrawl scrapes web content and supports MCP-compatible clients. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if firecrawl output is fed into aci or copied into its workflows. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is pasted or piped into aci prompts or MCP inputs, injected instructions can be interpreted as commands.
IF aci treats scraped text or emails as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any firecrawl output reaches aci.
Strip instructions from scraped text before passing it onward.
Use a fixed schema for inter-agent handoff messages.
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from web content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/content separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, calendar, and support data while firecrawl handles web content and API keys and has broad network egress. If either agent shares a workspace or forwards context to the other, sensitive business data can leave the intended boundary. Because both are network-capable and the pairwise isolation is undocumented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF aci and firecrawl share files, logs, or prompts, CRM/email data can be exposed to web-extraction flows.
IF firecrawl receives aci context containing customer data, that data can be transmitted off-box via its API calls.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials for each agent.
Redact CRM/email fields before any handoff to firecrawl.
Turn off verbose logging for both agents.
Review outbound destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad network egress, and both can call external APIs. That overlap creates contention on shared mutable resources such as OAuth-backed services, CRM records, or shared files if the operator co-locates them. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so conflict risk is real but not maximal.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same CRM or shared document without locks, last-write-wins conflicts can occur.
IF both agents use the same OAuth principal on shared services, overlapping mutations can race.
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts.
Limit one agent to read-only access where possible.
Stagger writes to shared systems.
Use optimistic concurrency checks on shared records.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions, and firecrawl can supply scraped web content or structured data that aci may consume. If firecrawl output is treated as authoritative by aci, errors or hallucinated facts can cascade into downstream business actions. The pair has no documented verification barrier, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is used as source data for aci without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF aci triggers emails, CRM updates, or calendar actions from unverified scraped data, downstream mistakes become operational.
mitigations: Require human approval before any action based on scraped data.
Cross-check firecrawl results against a second source.
Mark scraped fields as untrusted in handoff payloads.
Log source URLs alongside derived records.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: aci processes customer support, email, CRM, and calendar data, while firecrawl processes web content and API keys with broad egress. If EU or regulated customer data from aci is routed through firecrawl, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is plausible and should be treated as medium.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from aci is sent to firecrawl, retention and residency obligations may be violated.
IF firecrawl logs or stores request payloads longer than aci expects, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before any transfer between agents.
Block regulated fields from reaching firecrawl.
Confirm retention settings for both services.
Keep audit logs of cross-agent transfers.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies across the pair.
